advances: This proves absolute original-law second and third actual-depth moment bounds for every finite product of complete planar supports of lattice width at most two, allowing arbitrary support sizes, independently chosen tilts, lower-rank supports, and every proper-face entropy row. The product mean-cap argument uses regular scalar centers and spends its symmetric-noise factor only once. A support-uniform capacity surplus absorbs the averaged likelihood price. The result covers an infinite family of supports with no cardinality bound. It is a class-restricted theorem, not a final solution of the locked problem; no preservation of this class under an additional height lift or any mixed-integer consumer is asserted.
author: research-agent
proof:
We first fix the entropy identifications, affine coordinates, and boundary conventions. For a mean-\(\mathbf j\) law \(\eta\) on \(A_i\), log-affinity gives \(\sum_{\mathbf x}\eta_{\mathbf x}\log p_{i,\mathbf x}=\log p_{i,\mathbf j}\). Consequently \(D(\eta\|p_i)=-H(\eta)-\log p_{i,\mathbf j}\), where \(H(\eta):=-\sum_{\mathbf x}\eta_{\mathbf x}\log\eta_{\mathbf x}\). The unique relative-entropy minimizer is therefore the unique maximum-entropy mean-\(\mathbf j\) law. The boundary-inclusive entropy-capacity identity in bf1ff94487296374 yields

\[
\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j)
=e^{-D(\nu_{i,\mathbf j}\|p_i)}
=p_{i,\mathbf j}e^{H(\nu_{i,\mathbf j})}.
\]

That predecessor also gives positivity of \(\nu_{i,\mathbf j}\) on exactly \(E_{i,\mathbf j}\), and a finite exponential parameter on its face. In the notation of 53b9054891b43df0, this parameter is \(\boldsymbol\lambda_{i,\mathbf j}\): on \(E_{i,\mathbf j}\) the row is proportional to \(e^{\boldsymbol\lambda_{i,\mathbf j}\cdot(\mathbf x-\mathbf j)}\). It equals the source parameter \(\boldsymbol\ell_i\) plus the face multiplier of bf1ff94487296374; only its restriction to the face direction matters. Proper faces do not require a finite ambient optimizer for the capacity infimum. Capacities are positive because their defining sums contain the term \(p_{i,\mathbf j}>0\); all likelihood variances are finite on finite positive row supports. Hence every \(\omega_i\) is a probability law.

For completeness, the row of a product is exactly the product of these rows, even at boundary targets. Let \(\eta\) be any law on \(\prod_i A_i\) of mean \(\mathbf j\), and let \(\eta_i\) be its marginals. Direct expansion of the finite relative-entropies gives

\[
D(\eta\|P)
=D\!\left(\eta\middle\|\bigotimes_i\eta_i\right)
 +\sum_iD(\eta_i\|p_i)
\ge\sum_iD(\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\|p_i).
\]

The product of the marginals is positive wherever \(\eta\) is positive, so the first relative-entropy is well defined with zero terms omitted. Its nonnegativity follows from \(\log t\le t-1\). Equality is attained by \(Q_{\mathbf j}=\bigotimes_i\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\). Equality forces every marginal to be its unique minimizer and the joint law to be their product, proving uniqueness and the claimed identification. In particular its positive support is exactly \(\prod_iE_{i,\mathbf j_i}\).

For arbitrary finite positive product laws, not only the present class, the capacity exponential sum is the product of its block exponential sums. Every such product is at least the product of the positive block infima. Conversely, choose independently a vector approaching each block infimum, and then take a limit in this finite product. This proves the displayed capacity factorization, including nonattained boundary infima. Raising to power \(t\) and summing with the original product target probabilities proves the displayed \(\mathcal B_t\) factorization. The same identities apply to any grouped product below.

An invertible affine coordinate map on an affine hull preserves both quantities. For capacity, substitute the transpose linear map in the infimum. For depth, ambient halfspaces restrict either to intrinsic halfspaces or to the whole affine hull, and every intrinsic halfspace extends to an ambient one. A constant projection contributes probability one. These facts justify all intrinsic rank-one coordinates and every grouping of factors. Rank-zero supports are singletons and contribute no loss.

We next prove one mean cap for arbitrary mixtures of row ranks. Fix any target tuple and any original block normal \(\mathbf u=(\mathbf u_i)\). Let \(\mathbf X_i\) be independent with laws \(\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\); their means are \(\mathbf j_i\). We construct independent block pairs \((W_i,N_i)\), with each scalar center \(W_i\) centered, representing their original projections. Independence within a pair is not required.

If \(\dim F_{i,\mathbf j_i}=0\), the row is \(\delta_{\mathbf j_i}\), and take \(W_i=N_i=0\).

If \(\dim F_{i,\mathbf j_i}=1\), completeness identifies the entire face support as \(E_{i,\mathbf j_i}=\{\mathbf x_0+t\mathbf v:t=0,\ldots,m-1\}\), where \(\mathbf v\) is primitive and \(m=|E_{i,\mathbf j_i}|\). The target has an integral index \(j^{\mathrm{int}}\), so \(\mathbf j_i=\mathbf x_0+j^{\mathrm{int}}\mathbf v\). Its minimal-face rank one means this index is interior. Under this affine lattice map, the row is exactly the scalar geometric mean row \(\nu_{j^{\mathrm{int}}}\) of 075a3f88fa24d326 on its \(D=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\); its scalar mean label \(j\) is our \(j^{\mathrm{int}}\), and its scalar random coordinate \(X\) is our \(t\). Its unchanged row constant is \(K_{\mathrm{row}}\), while \(m\) here is interval cardinality, not an ambient dimension. Set \(W_i=(\mathbf u_i\cdot\mathbf v)(t-j^{\mathrm{int}})\) and \(N_i=0\). The accepted scalar fourth-moment inequality gives \(\mathbb EW_i^4\le K_{\mathrm{row}}(\mathbb EW_i^2)^2\), including a zero projection.

If \(\dim F_{i,\mathbf j_i}=2\), the row is positive on all of \(A_i\), complete, log-affine, and has integral vector mean. A width-one full-rank support cannot have such a row: a primitive integer functional of width one has extreme levels \(h,h+1\); positivity makes its expectation strictly between these two integers, whereas the expectation equals its integral value at \(\mathbf j_i\). Thus this case has width exactly two.

Apply 1232ba9a1c0673db with its original support \(D=A_i\), original law \(p=\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\), original tilt \(\boldsymbol\theta=\boldsymbol\lambda_{i,\mathbf j_i}\), and original vector mean \(\mathbf j=\mathbf j_i\). Its law label \(p\) therefore denotes our entropy row, not our original source \(p_i\). With its unimodular matrix \(T_i\), the exact normalized coordinates are \((S_i,Y_i)=T_i(\mathbf X_i-\mathbf j_i)\), and its normalized tilt is \((T_i^{-1})^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\lambda_{i,\mathbf j_i}\). The transformed row preserves every atom probability. Its support has the three nonempty integer columns at \(-1,0,1\). The original directional coefficients become

\[
\begin{pmatrix}a_i\\ b_i\end{pmatrix}
=(T_i^{-1})^{\mathsf T}\mathbf u_i,
\qquad
\mathbf u_i\cdot(\mathbf X_i-\mathbf j_i)=a_iS_i+b_iY_i.
\]

Use that fact's exact row realization, writing its scalar outer-branch probability \(\lambda\) as \(\lambda_{\mathrm{out},i}\), distinguished from the vector \(\boldsymbol\lambda_{i,\mathbf j_i}\). On the middle branch of probability \(1-\lambda_{\mathrm{out},i}\), sample its \(Y_{i,0}\), set \(C_{\mathrm{cen},i}=Y_{i,0}\), and set \((S_i,Y_i)=(0,Y_{i,0})\). On the outer branch, sample its independent vertical variables \(Y_{i,-},Y_{i,+}\) and an independent equiprobable sign \(\epsilon_i\), and set

\[
\begin{aligned}
C_{\mathrm{cen},i}&=\frac{Y_{i,-}+Y_{i,+}}2,\\
(S_i,Y_i)&=\left(\epsilon_i,
 C_{\mathrm{cen},i}+\epsilon_i\frac{Y_{i,+}-Y_{i,-}}2\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

These \(Y_{i,s}\), \(\lambda_{\mathrm{out},i}\), and \(C_{\mathrm{cen},i}\) are precisely the predecessor's \(Y_s,\lambda,C_{\mathrm{cen}}\) for this normalized row. Set \(W_i=b_iC_{\mathrm{cen},i}\). Take \(N_i=0\) on the middle branch and \(N_i=\epsilon_i[a_i+b_i(Y_{i,+}-Y_{i,-})/2]\) on the outer branch. Then the projection is exactly \(W_i+N_i\). The accepted center theorem gives \(\mathbb EW_i=0\) and \(\mathbb EW_i^4\le K_{\mathrm{cen}}(\mathbb EW_i^2)^2\). This is an inequality for the scalar center, not for the original planar projection.

Choose these realizations independently across every row. Since \(K_{\mathrm{cen}}\ge K_{\mathrm{row}}\) and \(K_{\mathrm{cen}}\ge3\), every constructed center satisfies \(\mathbb EW_i^4\le K_{\mathrm{cen}}(\mathbb EW_i^2)^2\). For \(W:=\sum_iW_i\) and \(v_i^{\mathrm{cen}}:=\mathbb EW_i^2\), independence and centering give

\[
\mathbb EW^4
=\sum_i\mathbb EW_i^4+6\sum_{i<h}v_i^{\mathrm{cen}}v_h^{\mathrm{cen}}
\le K_{\mathrm{cen}}\left(\sum_iv_i^{\mathrm{cen}}\right)^2
=K_{\mathrm{cen}}(\mathbb EW^2)^2.
\]

If \(\sigma^2:=\mathbb EW^2>0\), Hölder implies \(\mathbb E|W|\ge\sigma/\sqrt{K_{\mathrm{cen}}}\). Centering gives \(\mathbb EW_+=\mathbb E|W|/2\), and Cauchy--Schwarz yields \(\Pr(W\ge0)\ge(\mathbb EW_+)^2/\sigma^2\ge1/(4K_{\mathrm{cen}})\). If \(\sigma=0\), then \(W=0\) almost surely and the same lower bound holds.

Condition on every full-rank row's branch and sampled vertical variable or pair, and on the sampled variables of all rank-one rows, but not on the outer signs. This latent information determines \(W\). Given it, \(N:=\sum_iN_i\) is symmetric about zero: simultaneous negation of the independent equiprobable outer signs negates the noise, while all other noises are zero. Thus its conditional probability of being nonnegative is at least \(1/2\), including zero noise. On \(\{W\ge0,N\ge0\}\) the original projection sum is nonnegative. Therefore

\[
Q_{\mathbf j}\!\left\{\sum_i\mathbf u_i\cdot(\mathbf X_i-\mathbf j_i)\ge0\right\}
\ge\frac12\Pr(W\ge0)\ge\frac1{8K_{\mathrm{cen}}}=\delta.
\]

Every containing proper closed halfspace contains its parallel translate through the target. This proves \(\tau_{Q_{\mathbf j}}(\mathbf j)\ge\delta\) for every target, direction, and mixture of face ranks. When no full-rank rows occur the noises vanish; the displayed bound remains valid. In particular it includes every entropy tuple from width-one sources, where all rows are proper faces, even if the original support has more than four points. No directional fourth-moment hypothesis for the original width-two rows has been used.

We now convert this cap into actual original-law moments for the large planar factors. Set \(P_{\mathrm{big}}:=\bigotimes_{i\in I}p_i\) and \(R_{\mathrm{big}}:=\sum_{i\in I}r_i=2b\). The notation \(P_{\mathrm{big}}\) is exactly the big-source product notation of bf1ff94487296374 and c5abe3c72b8b89eb, now with large full-rank planar indices. By 20b9c918a887c030, every such original factor has \(\mathcal B_2(p_i)\ge g4^{-r_i}\). By 53b9054891b43df0, every factor in this class has the boundary-inclusive price bound \(\sum_{\mathbf j}\omega_{i,\mathbf j}V_{i,\mathbf j}\le V_0\). The latter theorem's \(A,p,r,F_{\mathbf j},E_{\mathbf j},\nu_{\mathbf j},V_{\mathbf j},\omega_{\mathbf j}\) are exactly our \(A_i,p_i,r_i,F_{i,\mathbf j},E_{i,\mathbf j},\nu_{i,\mathbf j},V_{i,\mathbf j},\omega_{i,\mathbf j}\). Its price retains the original face mass; no normalized face source is being substituted here.

Suppose \(b>0\), fix a big-product target tuple, and use its exact entropy product row \(Q_{\mathbf j}:=\bigotimes_{i\in I}\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\). Write \(v(\mathbf j):=\sum_{i\in I}V_{i,\mathbf j_i}\). On the positive support of this row put \(L_{\mathbf j}:=\log[Q_{\mathbf j}(\mathbf X)/P_{\mathrm{big}}(\mathbf X)]\). The entropy-capacity identity and independence give

\[
\mathbb E_{Q_{\mathbf j}}L_{\mathbf j}
=-\sum_{i\in I}\log\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j_i),
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_{Q_{\mathbf j}}L_{\mathbf j}=v(\mathbf j).
\]

When \(v(\mathbf j)>0\), Chebyshev bounds the event \(L_{\mathbf j}>\mathbb E L_{\mathbf j}+\sqrt{2v(\mathbf j)/\delta}\) by \(\delta/2\). When \(v(\mathbf j)=0\), use threshold zero and that strict exceptional event is empty. Intersect its complement with any containing halfspace, whose row mass is at least \(\delta\) by the mixed-row cap just proved. The intersection has row mass at least \(\delta/2=\alpha\). On it the exact density relation \(P_{\mathrm{big}}=Q_{\mathbf j}e^{-L_{\mathbf j}}\) gives, after summing and taking the infimum over the actual containing halfspaces,

\[
\tau_{P_{\mathrm{big}}}(\mathbf j)
\ge\alpha\exp\!\left[-\sqrt{\frac{2v(\mathbf j)}\delta}\right]
       \prod_{i\in I}\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j_i).
\]

All mass outside the positive row support is nonnegative and is left available in the original halfspace; it is not needed for this lower bound. This rederives the change-of-measure step of c5abe3c72b8b89eb with the proved product cap in place of that theorem's full-directional row fourth-moment certificate. Its theorem is not being applied with an uncertified original row.

Square and average with the original root probabilities of \(P_{\mathrm{big}}\). The exact algebraic capacity-weight law is \(\Omega:=\bigotimes_{i\in I}\omega_i\), yielding

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal M_2(P_{\mathrm{big}})
&\ge\alpha^2\sum_{\mathbf j}P_{\mathrm{big}}(\mathbf j)
       \left(\prod_{i\in I}\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j_i)^2\right)
       e^{-2\sqrt{2/\delta}\sqrt{v(\mathbf j)}}\\
&=\alpha^2\left(\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal B_2(p_i)\right)
       \mathbb E_{\Omega}e^{-2\sqrt{2/\delta}\sqrt{v(\mathbf j)}}.
\end{aligned}
\]

This \(\Omega\) is only the weight arising after the original-law depth moment has been formed. It is neither the original source law nor the entropy row used to measure halfspaces. Its tensorization is the displayed product identity, with no change to the original root probabilities.

The price bound and Cauchy--Schwarz give \(\mathbb E_{\Omega}\sqrt{v(\mathbf j)}\le\sqrt{\mathbb E_{\Omega}v(\mathbf j)}=\sqrt{\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb E_{\omega_i}V_{i,\mathbf j_i}}\le\sqrt{bV_0}\). Jensen's inequality for the convex decreasing function \(z\mapsto e^{-2\sqrt{2/\delta}z}\), applied to the nonnegative variable \(z=\sqrt{v(\mathbf j)}\), therefore implies

\[
\mathbb E_{\Omega}e^{-2\sqrt{2/\delta}\sqrt{v(\mathbf j)}}
\ge e^{-2\sqrt{2/\delta}\,\mathbb E_{\Omega}\sqrt{v(\mathbf j)}}
\ge e^{-2\beta\sqrt b}.
\]

This proves the required Jensen step for \(e^{-c\sqrt v}\) including atoms with \(v=0\), without differentiating at that endpoint. Substitution and the accepted surplus give

\[
\mathcal M_2(P_{\mathrm{big}})
\ge\alpha^2 e^{b\log g-2\beta\sqrt b}4^{-R_{\mathrm{big}}}
\ge a_2^2 4^{-R_{\mathrm{big}}},
\]

because \(b\log g-2\beta\sqrt b=\log g(\sqrt b-\beta/\log g)^2-\beta^2/\log g\ge-\beta^2/\log g\). If \(b=0\), this grouped product has moment one; since \(\alpha\le1\), both displayed lower bounds remain true, including the refined bound with \(b=0\).

We restore all rank-one original source factors as a single product with one constant. This requires checking the additional gain hypothesis in the scalar consumer of 075a3f88fa24d326; that fact alone does not assert a support-uniform gain. If \(r_i=1\), primitive intrinsic coordinates identify the original complete support as \(D_i=\{0,\ldots,m_i-1\}\), with \(m_i\ge2\). Its original law is geometric with scalar source tilt \(\theta_i=\boldsymbol\ell_i\cdot\mathbf v_i\), and unchanged atom probabilities. These are exactly the scalar source data \(D_i,p_i,\theta_i\) of 075a3f88fa24d326. Actual depth of their whole product is preserved under the product affine map described above.

For an arbitrary scalar geometric source \(p\) on \(D=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\) with \(m\ge3\), form the auxiliary complete planar rectangle \(\widetilde A=D\times\{0,1\}\) and the original log-affine law \(\widetilde p=p\otimes u\), where \(u\) is uniform on \(\{0,1\}\). This auxiliary law has tilt \((\theta,0)\), rank two, width one, and more than four sites. At the two binary targets the capacity is exactly \(1/2\), by the entropy formula or by taking the scalar exponential parameter to its endpoint limit. Hence \(\mathcal B_2(u)=1/4\). Applying the already proved exact capacity factorization and then 20b9c918a887c030 gives

\[
4\mathcal B_2(p)
=16\mathcal B_2(\widetilde p)\ge g.
\]

Thus the same absolute \(g\) supplies the scalar consumer's gain for every interval of length at least three and every tilt. No actual-depth statement about this auxiliary rectangle is used. For length two the baseline \(\mathcal B_2(p)\ge1/4\) follows from bf1ff94487296374.

Let \(P_1\) denote the single product of all original factors with \(r_i=1\), let \(R_1\) be their number, and let \(b_1\) count those with \(m_i\ge3\). With the exact scalar coordinate aliases just given, apply the conditional product conclusion of 075a3f88fa24d326, whose gain hypothesis was proved in the previous paragraph:

\[
4^{R_1}\mathcal M_2(P_1)
\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{row}}^2
 e^{b_1\log g-2\beta_{\mathrm{row}}\sqrt{b_1}}
\ge\alpha_{\mathrm{row}}^2e^{-\beta_{\mathrm{row}}^2/\log g}
=a_1^2.
\]

When there are no rank-one factors, \(P_1\) has moment one and the bound still holds since \(a_1\le1\). This restores arbitrarily many arbitrary-length intervals at a single constant cost, not a constant per factor.

It remains to restore the small full-rank planar factors and rank-zero factors. For any law on \(M\) atoms, every containing halfspace contains its target atom, so \(\tau_p(\mathbf j)\ge p_{\mathbf j}\) and \(\mathcal M_2(p)\ge\sum_{\mathbf j}p_{\mathbf j}^3\ge M^{-2}\); the last inequality is Jensen for the uniform average of these \(M\) masses. Thus every rank-two factor with \(|A_i|\le4\) has \(\mathcal M_2(p_i)\ge1/16=4^{-r_i}\), with no normalized prefactor loss and no entropy-row regularity requirement. Rank-zero factors have moment one.

Use the actual-depth supermultiplicativity of bf1ff94487296374. Explicitly, a halfspace through a product target has projection \(\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf X-\mathbf x)+\mathbf w\cdot(\mathbf Y-\mathbf y)\ge0\). It contains the product of the two events where the separate projections are nonnegative. Each has probability at least its block's actual depth, or probability one for a constant projection. Independence and translation of any containing halfspace through the target give \(\tau_{p\otimes q}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\ge\tau_p(\mathbf x)\tau_q(\mathbf y)\). Squaring and averaging with original product probabilities gives \(\mathcal M_2(p\otimes q)\ge\mathcal M_2(p)\mathcal M_2(q)\). Iterating for the grouping \(P_{\mathrm{big}},P_1\), the small planar factors, and the singleton factors gives

\[
4^R\mathcal M_2(P)
\ge a_1^2\alpha^2e^{b\log g-2\beta\sqrt b}
\ge a_1^2a_2^2=a^2.
\]

Finally, Jensen with the original target law \(P\) and the convex function \(z\mapsto z^{3/2}\) gives \(\mathcal M_3(P)=\mathbb E_P[(\tau_P(\mathbf j)^2)^{3/2}]\ge\mathcal M_2(P)^{3/2}\). Taking the power \(3/2\) of the refined second-moment bound proves exactly the stated refined third-moment bound, because \((4^{-R})^{3/2}=8^{-R}\). It also proves \(\mathcal M_3(P)\ge a^3 8^{-R}\).

Every target, including all proper-face targets, was retained in the original-law averages. The constants depend only on the absolute accepted scalar center, scalar likelihood, planar likelihood, and planar surplus constants. Support sizes, support geometry, all tilts, the number of factors, and the ranks of their target faces are unrestricted within the stated class. The source rank-zero case and constant projections were handled directly throughout. This proves the claimed infinite-family theorem without an all-row directional fourth-moment assumption and without any unrestricted planar or mixed-integer consequence.
statement:
All logarithms are natural. For every integer \(k\ge1\), let \(A_i\subseteq\mathbb Z^2\) be finite, nonempty, and complete, meaning \(A_i=\operatorname{conv}(A_i)\cap\mathbb Z^2\), and let \(r_i:=\dim\operatorname{aff}(A_i)\le2\). Whenever \(r_i=2\), assume lattice width at most two:

\[
\min_{\mathbf v\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{\mathbf0\}}
\left(\max_{\mathbf x\in A_i}\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf x
      -\min_{\mathbf x\in A_i}\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf x\right)\le2.
\]

For arbitrary \(\boldsymbol\ell_i\in\mathbb R^2\), put \(p_{i,\mathbf x}:=e^{\boldsymbol\ell_i\cdot\mathbf x}/\sum_{\mathbf y\in A_i}e^{\boldsymbol\ell_i\cdot\mathbf y}\), \(P:=\bigotimes_{i=1}^k p_i\), and \(R:=\sum_{i=1}^k r_i\). Use precisely the depth and capacity normalization of bf1ff94487296374:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_p(\mathbf j)
&:=\inf_{\substack{H\text{ a proper closed halfspace in the displayed ambient space}\\ \mathbf j\in H}}p(H),\\
\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)
&:=\inf_{\mathbf u}\sum_{\mathbf x}p_{\mathbf x}e^{\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf x-\mathbf j)},\\
\mathcal M_t(p)&:=\sum_{\mathbf j}p_{\mathbf j}\tau_p(\mathbf j)^t,
&\mathcal B_t(p)&:=\sum_{\mathbf j}p_{\mathbf j}\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)^t
\qquad(t=2,3).
\end{aligned}
\]

The order-two quantities are unchanged from that predecessor; the order-three extension is exactly that of c5abe3c72b8b89eb. The assignment's \(M_2,M_3\) are \(\mathcal M_2,\mathcal M_3\). A singleton has depth, capacity, and all these moments equal to one. An empty grouped product is interpreted as such a singleton embedded in a positive-dimensional ambient space.

For every \(\mathbf j\in A_i\), write \(F_{i,\mathbf j}\) for its minimal face in \(\operatorname{conv}A_i\), \(E_{i,\mathbf j}:=A_i\cap F_{i,\mathbf j}\), and \(\nu_{i,\mathbf j}\) for its mean-\(\mathbf j\) relative-entropy minimizing law against the original \(p_i\). This is exactly the row \(r_{i,\mathbf j}\) in bf1ff94487296374 and its maximum-entropy row \(r_{E_{i,\mathbf j},\mathbf j}\); it also coincides with the \(\nu_{i,\mathbf j}\) of c5abe3c72b8b89eb. Define, exactly as in 53b9054891b43df0 applied to source \(p_i\),

\[
V_{i,\mathbf j}:=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{i,\mathbf j}}
       \left[\log\frac{\nu_{i,\mathbf j}(\mathbf X_i)}{p_{i,\mathbf X_i}}\right],
\qquad
\omega_{i,\mathbf j}:=
\frac{p_{i,\mathbf j}\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j)^2}{\mathcal B_2(p_i)}.
\]

Likelihoods are evaluated only on the positive support of the row. The original target probabilities are \(p_{i,\mathbf j}\), never \(\omega_{i,\mathbf j}\).

Let \(g>1\) be the single absolute planar surplus constant of 20b9c918a887c030. Retain \(K_{\mathrm{cen}}=2^{18}(2400e^3)^2\) from 1232ba9a1c0673db and \(c_{\mathrm{lik},2}=16+2560K_{\mathrm{cen}}^2\) from 53b9054891b43df0. Set

\[
\begin{aligned}
\delta&:=\frac1{8K_{\mathrm{cen}}},
&V_0&:=16c_{\mathrm{lik},2},\\
\alpha&:=\frac\delta2,
&\beta&:=\sqrt{\frac{2V_0}{\delta}},
&a_2&:=\alpha\exp\!\left(-\frac{\beta^2}{2\log g}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

Here \(\alpha,\beta\) are new universal constants, not the fixed-family constants with these letters in bf1ff94487296374. Retain unchanged \(K_{\mathrm{row}}=20288\), \(c_{\mathrm{lik}}\), \(\alpha_{\mathrm{row}}=(8K_{\mathrm{row}})^{-1}\), and \(\beta_{\mathrm{row}}=\sqrt{8K_{\mathrm{row}}c_{\mathrm{lik}}}\) from 075a3f88fa24d326. Define \(a_1:=\alpha_{\mathrm{row}}\exp[-\beta_{\mathrm{row}}^2/(2\log g)]\) and \(a:=a_1a_2>0\). All these constants are absolute.

Then every stated product satisfies

\[
\mathcal M_2(P)\ge a^2 4^{-R},
\qquad
\mathcal M_3(P)\ge a^3 8^{-R}.
\]

More precisely, if \(I:=\{i:r_i=2,\ |A_i|>4\}\) and \(b:=|I|\), then

\[
\begin{aligned}
4^R\mathcal M_2(P)
&\ge a_1^2\alpha^2\exp\!\left(b\log g-2\beta\sqrt b\right)\ge a^2,\\
8^R\mathcal M_3(P)
&\ge a_1^3\alpha^3\exp\!\left(\tfrac32 b\log g-3\beta\sqrt b\right)\ge a^3.
\end{aligned}
\]

For every target tuple \(\mathbf j=(\mathbf j_i)\), its exact entropy row for the original product is \(Q_{\mathbf j}:=\bigotimes_i\nu_{i,\mathbf j_i}\), and \(\tau_{Q_{\mathbf j}}(\mathbf j)\ge\delta\), regardless of the ranks of the rows' minimal faces. Capacities and their moments factor exactly:

\[
\mathsf C_P(\mathbf j)=\prod_i\mathsf C_{p_i}(\mathbf j_i),
\qquad
\mathcal B_t(P)=\prod_i\mathcal B_t(p_i)\quad(t=2,3).
\]
